bottom_line: Stocks are getting hit hard as the AI trade cracks, while the Fed (the people who set interest rates) says inflation is still too high and is talking about raising rates, not cutting them. Both point to more expensive borrowing and a shakier market right now.

stories.real: The Dow dropped 1,100 points and the S&P 500 lost for the 6th straight day, the worst run since 2023. The Dow closed below 50,000 for the first time since June, led by tech and AI stocks falling.

stories.title: Fed wants more rate hikes
stories.real: Several Fed officials say inflation is 'way higher' than their 2% goal and back more rate hikes. Fed minutes say higher rates are needed in December, and J.P. Morgan expects hikes at the next three meetings. Officials agree on hiking but disagree on how fast.
stories.you: Higher rates usually mean credit cards, car loans and mortgages cost more to borrow on.

stories.title: Anthropic's record IPO, then a drop
stories.real: Anthropic pulled off the largest IPO on record (an IPO is when a company first sells shares to the public). Its stock jumped 27% on day one, then fell the next day as the wider market sank. There were also protests over its influence on AI.
stories.you: A hot first day on a new stock doesn't mean it stays up, as day two showed.

stories.title: Chip giants in trouble
stories.real: Nvidia is in a leadership crisis after Jensen Huang's departure, with California probing its AI chip sales to China and his legal exposure growing. A congressman says Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. AMD closed down over 7% after a short seller claimed China exposure, which AMD disputes.
stories.you: Chip makers are a big chunk of many tech and index funds, so their problems hit a lot of people's accounts.

stories.title: Investors run to safety
stories.real: Scared investors are piling into U.S. government bonds, which pushed Treasury yields (the interest those bonds pay) sharply lower. Gold went the other way, sliding near $3,500 an ounce, its lowest since September 2025, as rate-hike fears grow.
stories.you: Gold isn't acting as a safe spot right now, while government bonds are getting the fear money.
